pharm: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-alpha) agonist; lowers triglycerides and raises HDL via fenofibric acid
quick: 160 mg PO once daily (hypercholesterolemia); 54-160 mg once daily (severe hypertriglyceridemia)
Take with meals to optimize absorption
Use only if potential benefit justifies fetal risk; limited human data
Reduce dose; start 54 mg daily; contraindicated in severe renal impairment/dialysis
Lipid panel, liver enzymes, renal function, CBC; CK if myopathy suspected
summary: Fenofibrate is a fibrate (PPAR-alpha agonist) used as an adjunct to diet to lower elevated LDL-C, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and apolipoprotein B and to raise HDL-C in primary hypercholesterolemia or mixed dyslipidemia, and to treat severe hypertriglyceridemia. Its active form is fenofibric acid. It has not been shown to reduce coronary heart disease morbidity and mortality.
indications: Adjunct to diet to reduce elevated LDL-C, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and apolipoprotein B and to increase HDL-C in adults with primary hypercholesterolemia or mixed dyslipidemia
Adjunct to diet for treatment of adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia

dosage.d: 160 mg once daily (or equivalent formulation strength)
dosage.n: Place on lipid-lowering diet first and continue during treatment

dosage.d: Initial 54 to 160 mg once daily; maximum 160 mg once daily; titrate to response
dosage.n: Address obesity, alcohol intake, and contributory conditions first

dosage.d: Initial 54 mg once daily; increase only after evaluating effects on renal function and lipids
dosage.n: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment including dialysis

dosage.d: Select dose on the basis of renal function

admin: Place the patient on an appropriate lipid-lowering diet before and during therapy
Administer with meals to optimize bioavailability
Assess baseline and periodic lipid levels; discontinue if inadequate response after 2 months at maximal dose for hypertriglyceridemia
Evaluate renal function before dosing, especially in the elderly
Use the lowest effective dose and reassess periodically
moa: The active moiety is fenofibric acid, which activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-alpha). This increases lipolysis and clearance of triglyceride-rich particles by activating lipoprotein lipase and reducing apoprotein C-III. The lowered triglycerides shift LDL toward larger, buoyant, less atherogenic particles, and PPAR-alpha activation increases synthesis of apolipoproteins A-I and A-II and HDL-cholesterol. Fenofibrate also lowers serum uric acid.

absolute: Severe renal impairment, including dialysis patients
Active liver disease, including primary biliary cirrhosis and unexplained persistent liver function abnormalities
Known hypersensitivity to fenofibrate or fenofibric acid
relative: Concomitant statin therapy (increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis)
Mild to moderate renal impairment (dose reduction needed)

preg: There are limited human data. Animal studies showed adverse developmental effects at maternally toxic doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Fenofibrate is contraindicated in nursing mothers because of the potential for serious adverse reactions and possible tumorigenicity seen in animal studies. A decision should be made to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug.
renal: Fenofibrate is contraindicated in severe renal impairment, including patients on dialysis. In mild to moderate renal impairment, start at 54 mg once daily and increase only after evaluating effects on renal function and lipid levels. Monitor renal function, especially in the elderly, as exposure increases with reduced clearance.
hepatic: Fenofibrate is contraindicated in active liver disease, including primary biliary cirrhosis and unexplained persistent liver function abnormalities. It can increase serum transaminases; monitor liver enzymes and discontinue if levels persist above three times the upper limit of normal.

major: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins) - increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
Oral anticoagulants (warfarin) - potentiation of anticoagulant effect, monitor INR
moderate: Cyclosporine and other nephrotoxic immunosuppressants (increased risk of renal dysfunction)
Bile acid sequestrants (bind fenofibrate; take fenofibrate 1 hour before or 4-6 hours after)
minor: Drugs that are highly protein bound may be displaced
interactions.food: Take with meals to optimize bioavailability; excess alcohol intake contributes to hypertriglyceridemia and should be limited
interactions.alcohol: Excess alcohol intake can worsen hypertriglyceridemia; limit alcohol
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate serum transaminases and creatinine and lower uric acid; can affect lipid and liver test interpretation

rare: Severe hypersensitivity and cutaneous reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)
emergency: Rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine) - stop and seek emergency care
Acute pancreatitis (severe abdominal pain radiating to the back) - emergency care
Severe allergic skin reaction with blistering - emergency care

monitoring: Fasting lipid panel at baseline and periodically
Liver function tests at baseline and periodically; discontinue if persistently above 3x ULN
Serum creatinine and renal function, especially in the elderly and those on cyclosporine
Complete blood count periodically during the first 12 months
Creatine kinase if muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness occurs
counsel: Take with food and continue your prescribed low-fat diet, exercise, and weight management
Report muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially with fever or dark urine
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe stomach pain, or right-upper abdominal pain
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially statins and blood thinners
pk: Lipid effects develop over weeks; assess response after about 2 months
Fenofibric acid peaks at about 6-8 hours after an oral dose
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Active moiety is fenofibric acid; bioavailability improves when taken with food
Has not been shown to reduce coronary heart disease morbidity or mortality (limitation of use)
Most effective at lowering triglycerides and raising HDL; combining with statins raises myopathy risk
Contraindicated in severe renal impairment, active liver disease, gallbladder disease, and nursing mothers
Reduce dose in renal impairment and select dose by renal function in the elderly
missed: Take the missed dose with food as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Management is supportive with general symptomatic measures; fenofibrate is not appreciably eliminated by hemodialysis because of high protein binding. Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).
